title: Which MacBook Should You Buy in 2026?
summary: Apple's 2026 lineup has three clear tiers: the budget MacBook Neo, the mainstream MacBook Air and the high-performance MacBook Pro.
method: Picks come from Macworld and Tom's Guide buying guides, cross-checked with Envirofone and Refurbed comparisons. Only models covered by at least two of these sources are listed.
assumptions: Apple raised MacBook prices in 2026 (Macworld reports a $200 rise on the Air in June), so we show no prices here. Check the current price before you buy.

products.name: Apple MacBook Air 13-inch (M5, 2026)
why: Macworld names the 13-inch M5 Air the best MacBook overall and Tom's Guide calls it a fantastic laptop for most people. The M5 Air arrived in March 2026.
Tom's Guide reports battery life of over 15 hours, and Macworld notes it can drive two external displays.
specs: Memory and storage cannot be upgraded later
cons: RAM and storage are fixed, so buy the size you need up front
products.best_for: Students, professionals and anyone who wants one MacBook for everything
products.skip_if: You need sustained heavy workloads or the Pro's better display
products.amazon_listing: Apple 2026 MacBook Air 13-inch Laptop with M5 chip: Built for AI, 13.6-inch Liquid Retina
products.desc: A 13-inch MacBook Air with the Apple M5 chip and Wi-Fi 7, released in March 2026. Its memory and storage cannot be upgraded later.
products.benefit: Picture a student or professional carrying one light laptop from class to office to home, with a full day of battery. Macworld names it the best MacBook overall, Tom's Guide reports over 15 hours of battery, and it can drive two external displays. It is the best pick for most people in this guide, while the Neo is slower and the Pros cost much more. The catch: RAM and storage are fixed, so buy the size you need up front.

products.name: Apple MacBook Neo
why: Macworld calls the MacBook Neo the cheapest way to buy a Mac laptop in 2026, and Tom's Guide calls it an exemplary budget laptop for the price.
It uses the A18 Pro chip. Refurbed says the M5 in the Air has roughly double its multi-core and GPU performance, so it suits lighter use.
specs: About half the multi-core and GPU speed of the M5 Air (Refurbed)
cons: Less powerful than the Air and Pro
products.best_for: Budget buyers with light needs: browsing, schoolwork, email
products.skip_if: You edit video, code heavily or want the long-term headroom of the Air

products.desc: Apple's entry-level MacBook with the A18 Pro chip. It has about half the multi-core and GPU speed of the M5 Air (Refurbed).
products.benefit: Picture a student writing essays, browsing and sending email on a real MacBook. Macworld calls it the cheapest way to buy a Mac laptop in 2026, and Tom's Guide calls it an exemplary budget laptop for the price. It is the cheapest Mac in this guide. The catch: it is less powerful than the Air and Pro, so it is not for video editing or heavy coding.

products.name: Apple MacBook Pro 14-inch (M5)
why: Tom's Guide names the 14-inch M5 the best MacBook Pro overall: strong performance, long battery life and easy to carry.
Macworld recommends it for people who need sustained performance and better displays than the Air offers. Tom's Guide notes it is not a huge upgrade over the M4 model.
specs: Not a big jump from the M4 Pro-class model (Tom's Guide)
cons: Costs much more than the Air
products.best_for: Power users who want a dependable Pro that travels well
products.skip_if: Your work is light enough for the Air, or you need maximum GPU power

products.desc: A 14-inch MacBook Pro with the Apple M5 chip. It has a better display than the Air.
products.benefit: Picture a power user who carries a dependable Pro to client meetings, with strong sustained performance and long battery life. Tom's Guide names it the best MacBook Pro overall, and Macworld recommends it for people who need sustained performance and better displays than the Air offers. It is the Pro to pick if you do not need the M5 Pro or M5 Max. The catch: it costs much more than the Air.

products.name: Apple MacBook Pro (M5 Pro / M5 Max)
why: Macworld points creative pros, developers and high-end video editors to the M5 Pro and M5 Max Pros. Tom's Guide picks the M5 Pro for its strong GPU for video edits and AI work.
Refurbed names the 14-inch M5 Pro with 64 GB of memory the best configuration for photo and video creators.
specs: M5 Pro or M5 Max chip
Envirofone puts the 14-inch M5 at about £1,599 new, with M5 Pro/Max climbing past £3,000 (UK prices)
products.best_for: Video editors, developers and creative professionals
products.skip_if: You mostly browse, write and stream
products.desc: A 14-inch or 16-inch MacBook Pro with an M5 Pro or M5 Max chip. It is built for sustained heavy work, not for light use.
products.benefit: Picture a video editor or developer who runs heavy projects every day. Macworld points creative pros, developers and high-end video editors to the M5 Pro and M5 Max, and Tom's Guide picks the M5 Pro for its strong GPU for video edits and AI work. It has the top GPU and CPU power in this guide. The catch: it is very expensive and more than most people need.

verdict.line: If you want one MacBook for school, work and everything else, get this one: Macworld names it the best MacBook overall, and Tom's Guide reports over 15 hours of battery. Its memory and storage cannot be upgraded later, so buy the size you need up front.

tips.title: 4 mistakes when buying a MacBook
items: Treating the Neo like an Air.
Refurbed says the M5 in the Air has roughly double the multi-core and GPU performance of the Neo's A18 Pro chip.
Buying too little memory or storage on an Air.
The Air's RAM and storage are fixed, so you cannot upgrade them later.
Buying a Pro for light work.
If you mostly browse, write and stream, the Pro is more than you need.
Expecting a big jump from the 14-inch M5.
Tom's Guide notes the 14-inch M5 is not a huge upgrade over the M4 model.

faq: Which MacBook should most people buy?
The 13-inch M5 MacBook Air. Macworld names it the best MacBook overall, and Tom's Guide calls it a fantastic laptop for most people.
Is the MacBook Neo good enough?
For browsing, schoolwork and email, yes. Macworld calls it the cheapest way to buy a Mac laptop in 2026. Skip it if you edit video or code heavily.
When should I choose a MacBook Pro over an Air?
Choose a Pro if you need sustained performance and better displays than the Air offers, as Macworld says.
Which MacBook is best for video editors?
The MacBook Pro with M5 Pro or M5 Max. Tom's Guide picks the M5 Pro for its strong GPU for video edits and AI work.
Can I upgrade the memory later?
On the MacBook Air, no. Memory and storage cannot be upgraded after you buy.
